the_check_population_this_file_declares.the_bound_this_leaves: A file could declare a small check population, address many checks outside it, and report a flattering bucket 2. What stops that here is not the arithmetic: it is that the selector names an EXTERNAL anchor by scenario, that every declared check must be axis-decomposed before it counts (the generator refuses otherwise), and that the checks addressed outside are enumerated above rather than left silent. Stated as a residual, not papered over.
the_check_population_this_file_declares.the_9_vs_11_reconciliation: Two figures for CG1 exist and they disagree; stating which is which is the fix, and shipping both in silence is the defect. cg-reconciliation.md §3 records CG1 as MATCHED — 11 check keys, all `http-standard-headers`, 9 SUCCESS + 2 SKIPPED at the accepted run. This file declares 9. The difference is exactly `ClientMcpMethodHeader_initialize` and `ClientMcpMethodHeader_notifications_initialized`, and it is not a discrepancy: 11 is the MANIFEST figure (A1's 175) and 9 is the IN-DENOMINATOR one (the locator's 173, which is the unit this file's selector and every count in it use). Verified at this tip, and the coincidence is worth stating — those two keys are not merely excluded, they are THE WHOLE of A5's exclusion: bucket-0's own arithmetic is `in_denominator 173 + out_of_denominator 2 = 175`, and both of the 2 are these. A5 records each `removed_by_spec` — making them evaluate would need the client to send an `initialize` / `notifications/initialized` request, which 2026-07-28 removed under SEP-2575, so driving them would mean being LESS conformant. They are therefore not available as counterparts BY RULE, and the ET-CC members that would match them do not exist either.

what_a_record_carries_and_why.member: MES-67's unit: module AND test name. The `register_key` is docs/conformance/etcc-row-key.md §1's key and is what joins this file to the register; it was extracted from the register, never typed.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.claim: A3 §1's atom of matching — finer than a test, coarser than an assert. A member bundling claims contributes several edges and they are never collapsed.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.tag: A3 §5's token. The generator DECODES and RESOLVES it against A1's manifest and derives the six-field oc_key from the resolution; it never accepts a key from this file.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.axes: One verdict per axis of the check's predicate, naming axes that must exist in the check's axis decomposition (A3's 13 or C1's 11). The generator refuses an axis name the decomposition does not contain — a verdict against an axis nobody extracted is a verdict about nothing.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.et_verdict: The member's own run verdict. Every member of this population is `green`: re-measured at 42e6b19 over the full suite, all 281 ET-CC members pass. So buckets 3 (green OC / red ET) and 6 (red in both) are EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION on this data — checked, and zero, with the predicate recorded.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.evidence: File, line and the assertion, for every axis verdict. Ruling 7: an address is not evidence, the bytes at it are.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.not_carried: No `oc_key`, no `shape`, no `bucket`, no OC verdict. All four are derived — the OC verdict from A1's committed per-check `status` at the accepted run, the rest through MatchKey.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.the_search_that_found_none: On every declared_unmatched record C1b-i and C1b-ii authored: what was read, and what it said. A verdict of 'no counterpart' with no search behind it is a silence wearing a token (A2d). C1a's five inherited records predated this field; C1b-i stated that rather than backfilling, since backfilling would have been inventing the search. C1b-ii RAN the search for the three CG2 ones and added the field to them, attributed and dated in `field_added_by`. The two CG7 records at indices 3 and 4 still predate it and are still left stated rather than invented — their search is a fixture read, and C1b-ii did not run it.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.why_no_counterpart: Which of the two reason-slugs applies and why. `no-oc-scenario` — the suite has no such check ANYWHERE, so the search is over all 173. `no-oc-fixture-case` — the scenario exists and is matched, but its fixture holds no case that would exercise the constraint, so the search is over the fixture.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.the_near_miss_that_is_not_a_counterpart: On a bucket-1 record whose search returns zero but where a nearby artefact uses the same WORD in another sense. A zero with its near miss named is a search; a bare zero is a grep that a later reader will re-run, find the word, and mistrust.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.claim_the_slot_names: MES-77: an `oc:none` native id names a CLAIM, not a member. The field spells that claim out, so the slug is readable and two members discharging one claim is visibly deliberate rather than a collision.

how_a_silent_axis_was_decided: Conservatively, and the rule is stated rather than applied case by case: a claim counts as covering an axis only when an assertion's SUBJECT is the behaviour that axis names. A test asserting a tool's RESULT does not cover an axis about the ARGUMENTS' wire type, and a test asserting that a capability is ABSENT does not cover an axis about the SHAPE of a present one. This is match-relation.md §6's CG5 rule — a mention is not a discharge — turned on our own side of the relation. Where it was a judgement rather than a reading, the edge's `evidence` says so in those words.
the_all_silent_case: Four edges have EVERY axis silent. They are recorded and ESCALATED, never bucketed. A3 §2 rules that covering zero of one axis 'is no match, not a partial one'; generalised to N axes that is exactly this case, and A3 §3's table has no row for it — `shape_from_axes/1` would call it `:partial` and bucket 5 would swallow it. Dropping the edges instead would be worse: the member would then look edge-less and therefore bucket-1, asserting 'we looked and there is no counterpart' where the truth is 'there is a counterpart and our claim does not touch its predicate'. Escalation is A3 §7's own mechanism for a case the rule does not decide.
what_unmatched_means_in_a_file_that_decl: A3 §6 state 3 reads absolutely — the member has NO OC counterpart. In a file whose check population is a declared subset it can only mean 'no counterpart among the checks this file declares', and the difference is not pedantic. C1b-i recorded two CG7 members whose claims' counterparts lived in CG1's `http-standard-headers`, outside its population; C1b-ii declares CG1, so those are now real edges — which is the mechanism working, and the reason the two kinds of absence were kept apart rather than collapsed. What remains genuinely absent is recorded as such, with the search.
claims_without_an_edge_note: A3's state 3 is a property of a MEMBER, and a member is either edge-bearing or declared unmatched — the generator's bucket-1 reconciliation requires exactly that. So a member that matches on some claims and not on others has nowhere to put the unmatched ones. C1b-i found five and ESCALATED them; whether A3 §6 should gain a claim-level state 3 is MES-110's, not this file's. C1b-ii's disposition of those five, and its own finding, are: TWO became real edges — the tools_call Method and Name claims C1b-i routed here by name, whose counterparts are inside this file's declared 10 now that CG1 is declared. Their claim-level RECORDS were REMOVED, not left beside the new edges: a claim that is both an edge and a claim-without-an-edge is a contradiction in the file, and nothing guards it — `claims_without_an_edge` is reported by count and by row, and a duplicate would have inflated the escalation figure while the edge quietly discharged the same claim. The removal is the completion of C1b-i's routing, and the rows are recoverable from C1b-i's commit (545f48b). TWO were `unowned — recommend it to C1b-ii with CG1`, and C1b-ii ran the search over the real 10 and CONFIRMED both, recording WHY in `resolved_by` rather than passing the recommendation on again; a recommendation no later ticket answers is how these rot. ONE — the SEP-2243 SHOULD-log with no OC check on either leg — is untouched and remains a MES-110 case. C1b-ii adds ONE new case of its own, the no-Mcp-Name-on-a-non-name-bearing-method claim, escalated the same way and not force-bucketed.
